decisions.reason: Korean idiom 입만 바라보다 conveys eager dependence on his words; SOL's "hanging on his every word" renders that effect while BASE's "watching his lips" is a literal calque.

"이 갑자" is the demonstrative (this jiazi), not "two"; with his age already near 백수, BASE's "two jiazi" (=120 years) is wrong. SOL also drops the unsupported "manifested" for 강기, keeps Supreme Peak, and anchors the jiazi footnote.
"Ugh. I can't stand watching this" matches 에잉 / 답답해서 안 되겠다 more idiomatically than BASE's "Good grief… making me frustrated."
"Don't 'elder' me" captures the metalinguistic complaint in 어르신 같은 소리 하고 있네; BASE's "Don't call me elder" is flatter.
Korean is about speech (입 벙긋… 말 한마디) and is plural (죽는다, "we die"); BASE's "if I put one foot wrong, he'll kill me" changes both the mechanism and the subject.
The Korean line has no vocative; BASE's added "sir" is an unsupported address term, while 소인 is a humble self-reference that need not be carried over.
Korean explicitly says 금 (gold); BASE drops it, and SOL's "even if you paid gold for it" is also more natural.
SOL preserves the intensifier 시원치 않아 ("even that wouldn't be enough"), which BASE omits.
Korean is 절대 고수 (peerless master), not the rank 초절정; BASE substitutes the glossary rank term "Supreme Peak," which the source does not use here.
SOL preserves the familiar hail 이보게 ("Hey") that BASE drops, and uses the project's space-free em dash.
